Starting from rest, an object rolls (without slipping) down along an incline that rises by 3 in every 5 (along it). The object gains a speed of √10 m/s as it travels a distance of 5/3 m along the incline. What can be the possible shape/s of the object? (Take g = 10 m/s².)
book_key: k²/R² = 1 → a ring or a hollow cylinder

stem: A body is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface and its rotational kinetic energy is equal to the translational kinetic energy. The body is (a) Disc (b) Sphere (c) Cylinder (d) Ring —

A solid sphere of mass M and radius R is placed on top of a rough inclined surface of height h. It rolls down the incline without slipping. Its kinetic energy on reaching the bottom of the incline will be: (a) Mgh (b) Less than Mgh as the surface is rough (c) More than Mgh because of additional rotational kinetic energy (d) Depending on the coefficient of static friction between the sphere and the surface. —

For a hollow cylinder and a solid cylinder rolling without slipping on an inclined plane, then which of these reaches earlier on the ground? (a) Solid cylinder (b) Hollow cylinder (c) Both simultaneously (d) Can't say anything —

answer: a The velocity of highest point is 2V_cm and point of contact is zero
stem: A disc is rolling, the velocity of its centre of mass is V cm . Then which one will be correct? Find the speed (in m/s) of COM of cylinder when it reaches the bottom. (Take g = 10 m/s².)

A solid sphere of mass 2 kg rolls (without slipping) on a horizontal surface at 10 m/s and then rolls up an inclined plane of inclination 30°; find to which height (in m) it rolls? (Take g = 10 m/s².)

A particle starts from rest and moves along a circle of radius (20/π) m with constant tangential acceleration. If the velocity of the particle is 80 m/s at the end of second revolution after motion has begun, then find the tangential acceleration (in m/s²).

answer: v_C = mv/(M + m), along the particle's initial velocity
stem: A uniform rod of length L and mass M lies on a smooth horizontal table. A particle of mass m moving on the table with speed v strikes the rod perpendicularly at one end and sticks to the rod after the collision. Find the velocity of the centre of mass C of the system constituting “the rod plus the particle”.
book_key: v C = mv/(M + m), along the particle's original direction

stem: A small sphere (solid) rolls down without slipping from rest at the top of a track in a vertical plane. The track has an elevated section and a horizontal part. B where the sphere lands (B is vertically below the end of the horizontal part). (Take g = 10 m/s².)

The friction coefficient between the 2.0 kg block and the plane below it is 0.5 and the plane below the 4.0 kg block is frictionless. Calculate the acceleration of the 4.0 kg block. The string does not slip on either. Find the tension in the part of the string joining the wheel and the pulley. (Take g = 9.8 m/s².)

At this moment, kinetic energy of rod is (the rod makes 45° with the floor and its lower end moves along the floor with speed V 0 ) (a) mv 0 ² (b) (1/3)mv 0 ² (c) ½mv 0 ² (d) ¼mv 0 ² —

What will be the maximum height (from initial position) reached by A on B? (a) 3v²/4g (b) v²/4g (c) v²/2g (d) v²/3g —

If initially it had kinetic energy of 4 J, find the ratio of kinetic energy due to translation and rotation at maximum height of its trajectory (mass of disc is 0.1 kg; take g = 10 m/s²).
